newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile inmate relatives occupy Australian embassy.
newsitem.headline: Chile inmate relatives occupy Australian embassy.

text.p: Four relatives of jailed left-wing guerrillas peacefully occupied the Australian Embassy in Chile on Thursday and said they were on a hunger strike to demand better prison conditions for their relatives.

The four unarmed people, at least three of them women, entered the embassy's visa section and refused to leave, erecting banners outside demanding an end to prison abuses and shouting slogans to reporters outside.

All four had begun a hunger strike inside the embassy and other relatives gathered outside. The action was peaceful and they did not attempt to damage the embassy in any way, said an embassy official who asked not to be identified.

"We've told the Chilean authorities we don't think this requires any action. We've asked them to reduce the normal police presence outside to one officer, and they have done that," he said. "These people have come to make a point. We're just going to let them stew in their juices for a while."
Embassy officials were not offering them water or talking to them, he added.
Chile's acting foreign minister, Mariano Fernandez, said Chilean authorities would act in accordance with requests by the Australian government, represented in Santiago by Ambassador Ken Berry.
Authorities gave no immediate reason why the strikers chose to occupy the Australian rather than another embassy.
Embassy officials said the sit-in was by three women and one man. But Fernandez and supporters of the protesters outside said there four women.

All four said they were relatives of "political prisoners" in two Santiago jails, including the maximum security prison where four guerrillas escaped last month with the help of a helicopter piloted by their comrades.
The relatives demanded the government lift a ban on prison visits and relax tight restrictions on outdoor time for the inmates, measures imposed after the Dec. 30 prison escape.
"This is a peaceful occupation and hunger strike to demand an end to abuses of our husbands and the restitution of visits," Irma Veliz, wife of jailed guerrilla Guillermo Ossandon, told Reuters.
Veliz said 55 inmates inside the maximum security jail in central Santiago had also begun a hunger strike to coincide with those in the embassy.
